note: D5/D6 are one moment with two real slips (D3 grammar صلحني -> صلح لي; vocab صلح -> ساعدني) - I assigned D5 = grammar, D6 = vocab so they do not duplicate. Invented broken plurals (D8, D14) filed as vocab tier 2 per the reader brief; singular-for-plural (D12) as grammar A9. Rule questions (D18, D22, D23) dropped per the 2026-10-01 rule.

rulings.why: Not an error: the transcript cannot show a shadda, and Amal's repeat وجهّزت كباب is her habit of echoing a right sentence - Medi cites this very moment at 04:36 ('you made kebab') as an example of her repeating something he said correctly.

row.medi_said: سـ... تلات إلا نـ... إلا تلت.
row.why: Asked the time, he gave تلات (three) for the hour; Amal queried 'three or two?', he changed to تنتين إلا تلت and she repeated it. Low: the real clock time is not in the transcript, so it may be a fact slip rather than a word slip.

rulings.why: Amal's question 'تلات أو تنتين؟' is a voiced prompt and he switched to her number; kept low because the real time cannot be checked.

row.medi_said: كراجي. See, This is a new word.
row.why: He garbled the word Amal had given at 09:10 (كهربجي, also said as كرهبجي at 09:30); she recast it syllable by syllable. He attempted it, so not tier 0; wrong form of a word just given = tier 2.

rulings.why: He attempted the word and mangled it, Amal recast - tier 2, not a didn't-know (tier 0 is for a word he never tried).

row.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- لا، أه، كهربجي، هو مهندس
row.why: He meant 'he is not an electrician, he is an engineer': a noun is negated with mish and no 'to be' verb (مش كهربجي); he built ما يكون. Best reading of a halting turn; Amal let it pass.
row.english: he's not an electrician, he's an engineer

rulings.why: Both readers saw the slip; the sentence contrasts with present هو مهندس, so present negation of a noun (C4, مش) fits better than past ما كان (B6).

row.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. Like you, you were who's being fixed. ... Fixed for me، صلح لي.
row.why: 'for me' rides on the preposition la- with an ending (صلح لي), not on the verb as its object (صلحني = he fixed ME); Amal explained the difference out loud.
row.english: he fixed it for me a bit

rulings.why: Same moment holds TWO real slips; D5 and D6 are the same pair with labels swapped. I rule D5 = the grammar slip (صلحني -> صلح لي, D3) and D6 = the vocab slip (صلح -> ساعدني) so neither is duplicated.

row.medi_said: صلح لي, helps to me, شوي.
row.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me? ... ساعدني.
row.why: He used صلح (fix) meaning 'he helped me' (he said 'helps to me'); Amal asked if he meant help and he produced ساعدني, which she repeated (sheet: help | Saa3ed | ساعد).

rulings.why: See D5: this is the second, separate slip of the same moment - the wrong verb.

row.why: For 'I stayed' the doubled verb dall takes the -ait ending (ضلّيت, sheet: i stayed/kept | Ana dallait); he said a dallet-type form (engine wrote دولت), Amal did not recognise it ('what?') and gave ضليت, he repeated it. The verb is right, only the past ending is wrong, so grammar not vocab.

rulings.why: The word is right (ضل), only the past ending is off - a B5 ending rule, so grammar per the brief, not tier 2.

row.why: He said ayoom for the broken plural ayyaam; Amal supplied أيام and he took it ('I even wrote أيام'). The brief puts an invented plural shape under vocab tier 2 (the fix is a pattern, not an ending rule). Could be only a vowel slip.

rulings.why: Broken-plural shape wrong; the reader brief lists 'wrong plural pattern he invented' as vocab tier 2.
Repeat of the line Amal just fixed (GR-28): within 3 s he echoed her bare word أيام; his own line at 20:41 had el- (هدول الأيوم). Not a fresh slip.

row.why: He named K-S-R then said بخسر (a different word, 'I lose') for بكسر 'I break'; Amal said 'close' and gave بكسر. Kept as tier 2 to match the agreed كسر/سكر letter-swap rows (A19, A21, A24, A29).

rulings.why: Same family as the agreed letter-swap rows; she voiced the fix, so it stays vocab-A tier 2.

row.why: After بتضلي the second verb needs its person prefix; he said bare كسري three times, Amal recast بتكسري and said she did not hear the t, he fixed to بتكسري at 33:31. The missing piece she named is the t (person), so B18; the b- is the second issue.

rulings.why: Amal named the missing t, so B18 is the main bucket; B1 as second id.

row.why: 'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he used the singular كاسته, Amal recast and he said 'كاساته، of course'. Choosing singular for plural is a number slip (A9), not an invented word form.

rulings.why: He knows both forms (he says 'of course'); singular used for plural = A9 grammar.

row.why: For هو the verb is بينكسر without the feminine -i; Amal moved on to إنتو without fixing it. Low: could be the engine carrying the -i from the previous إنتي بتنكسري line.

rulings.why: Real agreement slip in a conjugation drill that Amal let pass (her next word إنتو just moves the drill on).

row.medi_said: إن إن. الفـ--، الفـ--، علات، الفعلات إن.
row.why: He invented the plural fe3laat for fe3el; Amal gave the broken plural أفعال and he said الأفعال. Invented plural pattern = vocab tier 2 per the brief.

rulings.why: Invented plural pattern; brief puts this under vocab tier 2.

row.why: For 'I am annoyed' he said مزعج (annoying); his 'No.' gave no right word before Amal supplied أنا مزعوج, then he confirmed مزعج = annoying. Sheet: annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج; annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج. Same root, wrong participle of a word he knows (he said مزعوج at 18:41) = tier 2.

rulings.why: Not a self-fix (no right word before hers); wrong participle of a known word = tier 2.

row.why: Amal asked كيف الجو عندكم اليوم in the afternoon and he answered 'tonight' (الليلة); best reading is he meant today. Could be the engine or a real 'tonight'; she let it pass.

rulings.why: Plausible wrong word she let pass; vocab-B goes to her review, kept low.

row.why: Sheet: 'i call | Ana barenn (3ala)' - rann takes 3ala, he used la-; Amal was busy with the electricity word and let it pass.

rulings.why: Fixed preposition of rann is 3ala (sheet); she let it pass.
A question about the form ('Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟'), not a slip (Medi 2026-10-01 rule); also مهندس كهربا (an electrical engineer) is itself fine, Amal just gave the common phrase.

row.why: She asked for 'you (f) got annoyed with me'; he stalled in English and she supplied انزعجتي one second later - a didn't-know, not a slip.

rulings.why: Amal supplied the form before any attempt = didn't-know, tier 0.

row.why: He asked how to say 'one more' with a word-for-word guess (aktar); Amal gave كمان واحد (sheet: one more time | Kaman marra) and he repeated. Framed as a how-do-you-say question, so a didn't-know (tier 0).

rulings.why: It is a 'how do you say' question with a guess; brief files that as vocab-A tier 0 asked.

row.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
row.why: 'The beginning of the word' is awal el-kelme - no el- before awal (A13); he put el- on awal both times. Low: he often uses a bare الـ as a filler, so the first الـ may be a pause (S5). Amal only said Mm.
row.english: the beginning of the verb / word

rulings.why: Repeated el- before awal in both phrases suggests a real A13 slip, but filler الـ is possible - kept low.
A question about the form ('نكسر؟ Is it نكسر؟'), not a use (Medi 2026-10-01 rule); also nkasar vs inkasar differs only by the initial glide the engine often drops.

A question about the form: he asked 'كان عمرها or عمرها كان?' then 'كانت، right?' and Amal answered لأ - a rule question is neither slip nor use (Medi 2026-10-01 rule). His real sentence at 43:47 used كان عمرها correctly.

row.medi_said: air condition-ي، air conditioner-ي. Do I say for air condition?
row.why: A borrowed English noun takes 'my' with taba3i, not the -i ending; he produced the -i form first, then asked, and Amal gave the taba3i form, which he used at 48:31 and 53:14. Low because the attempt turned into a question.

rulings.why: He produced the wrong form before asking, and she recast it - kept, low.
Not a correction: he was listing the verb pair ('آخر فعل is... بنكسر. أكسر.') and Amal confirmed with 'بكسر and بنكسر. صح.' - naming, not using the verb; the bare أكسر may be the engine.

He asked 'انكسر؟' and Amal said at 49:51 'You would use انكسر' if it really broke; she only explained the خرب option - not clearly a correction of a wrong word.
